statement: The program must write a text report named acadinfo.txt containing general user, computer and platform information, loaded application modules, and system variable settings for troubleshooting and comparing installations.
notes: Added from help page "ACADINFO (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run ACADINFO; a file acadinfo.txt is created that lists the user name, loaded modules and the current values of system variables.

statement: The program must provide an alias editor that adds, edits and removes command aliases and shell command aliases stored in the PGP file, with confirm, apply and close behavior.
notes: Added from help page "ALIASEDIT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open ALIASEDIT, add alias ZZ for ZOOM and apply; typing ZZ at the command line starts ZOOM and the PGP file contains the new entry.

statement: The program must create text that follows a selected arc through a workshop dialog with options for text, font and style, color, height, width factor, spacing, offsets from the arc and ends, and position relative to the arc.
notes: Added from help page "ARCTEXT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run ARCTEXT, pick an arc, enter text and set an offset of 2; an arc-aligned text object follows the arc offset by 2 units and moves with it when the arc moves.

statement: The program must provide the ATTIN express tool that reads a tab-delimited file written by ATTOUT and updates attribute values on the block references identified by the HANDLE and BLOCKNAME columns, then offers interactive assignment for rows it could not match.
notes: Added from help page "ATTIN (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Export attributes with ATTOUT, change one value in the text file, run ATTIN on it, and assert the matching block's attribute now has the new value and other blocks are unchanged.

statement: The program must provide the ATTOUT express tool that prompts for a file name and block names, then writes the attributes of the chosen blocks as a tab-delimited text file with HANDLE and BLOCKNAME header columns for later re-import with ATTIN.
notes: Added from help page "ATTOUT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run ATTOUT on a drawing with two block types, select one block name; assert the output file has a header row starting with HANDLE and BLOCKNAME and one row per reference of that block.

statement: The program must provide the obsolete BEXTEND express tool that extends objects to a boundary taken from a block or from objects inside a block reference.
notes: Added from help page "BEXTEND (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Insert a block containing a vertical line, draw a horizontal line short of it, run BEXTEND selecting the block as edge then the line; assert the line's endpoint lies on the block's line.

statement: The program must provide the BLOCK? express tool that lists the entity data of a block definition, chosen by name or by picking a reference, optionally limited to one entity type.
notes: Added from help page "BLOCK? (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run BLOCK? for a block containing a line and text, enter type LINE; assert only the line's entity data is listed, then press Enter for all and assert both appear.

statement: The program must provide the BLOCKTOXREF express tool that replaces every instance of a named block with a reference to a specified external drawing, with a command-line variant, so that the block definition can then be purged.
notes: Added from help page "BLOCKTOXREF (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Insert block PART twice, run BLOCKTOXREF PART with file part.dwg; assert both references now point to an xref of part.dwg and PURGE removes the unused PART definition.

statement: The program must provide the BREAKLINE express tool that draws a polyline between two points with a breakline symbol block at a chosen position, with options for the symbol block, symbol size and extension beyond the points, scaled by DIMSCALE.
notes: Added from help page "BREAKLINE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run BREAKLINE from 0,0 to 10,0 with default options; assert a polyline with the symbol block is created, and with DIMSCALE 48 assert the symbol is 48 times larger than at DIMSCALE 1.

statement: Provide an Express Tool command that rescales selected block references about their insertion points with separate X, Y and Z factors, applied either as final absolute values or as multipliers on the current scale.
notes: Added from help page "BSCALE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Insert a block at scale 1,1,1, run BSCALE in Absolute mode with X=3 and Y left as the X value, and assert the reference reports X and Y scale 3.

statement: Provide the obsolete Express Tool that trims or, with shift-select, extends objects using a block or the contents of a block reference as the cutting boundary, with the usual Fence, Crossing, Project, Edge, eRase and Undo choices.
notes: Added from help page "BTRIM (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a line crossing a block reference, run BTRIM selecting the block as the edge and pick the line on one side, and assert the line is cut at the block outline.

statement: Provide an Express Tool command that explodes selected block references so the pieces land on the block's layer rather than their original layers, while attribute values become ordinary text objects placed on the layer and in the text style of the original attribute definition.
notes: Added from help page "BURST (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Burst a block holding an attribute with value A12 and a line originally on layer X, and assert the line is on the block layer and a text object reading A12 exists on the attribute definition's layer.

statement: Provide an Express Tool that reorders the display order of selected objects according to a user-ordered list of color numbers, placing the listed colors in front of or behind unlisted objects, optionally recursing into blocks, with a command-line variant (-CDORDER).
notes: Added from help page "CDORDER (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a red and a blue circle that overlap, set the priority list with red first and Front, run CDORDER, and assert red draws above blue in the draw order.

statement: Provide an Express Tool that lets the user edit a URL previously attached to selected objects, stepping through each URL when several are selected.
notes: Added from help page "CHURLS (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Attach a URL to a rectangle, run CHURLS, change the address to a new one, and assert the stored URL on the object is updated.

statement: Provide an Express Tool that clips blocks, xrefs, images and wipeouts using polylines, circles, arcs, ellipses or text as boundary, approximating curves by short segments governed by a maximum error distance.
notes: Added from help page "CLIPIT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Clip an xref with a circle using error 0.1, and assert the clip boundary is a polygon whose segment midpoints deviate from the circle by at most 0.1.

statement: Provide an Express Tool that copies objects repeatedly using Repeat, linear Divide, linear Measure and Array (Pick, Measure, Divide) modes, taking points by coordinates, grid snap or object snap but not by typed direct distance.
notes: Added from help page "COPYM (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run COPYM on a circle with Divide using a second point 10 units away and 4 copies, and assert four evenly spaced copies result.

statement: The Express Tools DIMEX command must write chosen named dimension styles to an external ASCII DIM file, with a choice of storing full text-style data or only the text style name.
notes: Added from help page "DIMEX (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: With two dimension styles defined, run DIMEX selecting both and Text Style Name Only, and assert the resulting DIM file exists and lists both styles.

statement: The Express Tools DIMIM command must load all dimension styles and their text styles from a DIM file made by DIMEX into the current drawing, offering to either keep or overwrite same-named existing styles.
notes: Added from help page "DIMIM (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Import a DIM file containing style A while A already exists with different settings; assert Keep leaves A unchanged and Overwrite replaces A with the imported values.

statement: The Express Tools DIMREASSOC command must restore the real measured value to dimension text that was overridden or edited by hand.
notes: Added from help page "DIMREASSOC (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a dimension of 10 units with its text overridden to 99, run DIMREASSOC on it, and assert the displayed text equals the measured 10.

statement: The Express Tools DUMPSHX utility must decompile SHX font and shape files, including big font and Unifont files, into readable SHP source with options for decimal character codes and an output file name.
notes: Added from help page "DUMPSHX (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run dumpshx -o simplex.shp simplex.shx and assert the SHP file is produced and recompiles to an equivalent SHX.

statement: The Express Tools DWGLOG command must toggle per-drawing history logging that records who opened, closed or attached each drawing, with a time stamp, in a DWH file beside the drawing.
notes: Added from help page "DWGLOG (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Turn DWGLOG on, open and close a drawing, and assert a DWH file contains Opened by and Closed by entries with user, machine and time.

statement: The Express Tools EDITTIME command must track active editing time per drawing with On, Off, Reset and an inactivity Timeout, and expose the total through the stored drawing data and LISP functions.
notes: Added from help page "EDITTIME (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Turn EDITTIME on with a 1-minute timeout, idle past it and assert timing suspends; Reset and assert the total is zero.

statement: The Express Tools EXOFFSET command must offset objects by distance or through a point with layer control, undo, a multiple mode and OFFSETGAPTYPE-based corner handling.
notes: Added from help page "EXOFFSET (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run EXOFFSET with Layer set to Current on a source object on another layer, offset 5, and assert the new object is on the current layer.

statement: The Express Tools EXPLAN command must show the plan view of a chosen UCS centered on selected objects while keeping the current magnification, with the same options as PLAN.
notes: Added from help page "EXPLAN (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run EXPLAN at a given zoom factor, and assert the view becomes plan with the same view height as before.

statement: The Express Tools EXPRESSMENU command must add the Express pull-down to the menu bar, optionally rebuilding it first, within the limit on menu entries.
notes: Added from help page "EXPRESSMENU (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run EXPRESSMENU and assert the Express menu appears on the menu bar with its tools.

statement: The Express Tools EXPRESSTOOLS command must load the Express libraries, add the Express folder to the search path and add the Express pull-down to the menu bar so they load at each later startup.
notes: Added from help page "EXPRESSTOOLS (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run EXPRESSTOOLS in a profile without them and assert the Express menu appears and the tools load on the next launch.

statement: The Express Tools EXTRIM command must trim all objects crossing a selected cutting edge (a polyline, line, circle, arc, ellipse, or a text-type object including attribute definitions) on the side of a picked point in one operation.
notes: Added from help page "EXTRIM (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a circle as the edge, pick a point inside it, and assert every line crossing the circle is trimmed back to the circle on the inside.

statement: The Express Tool FS must gather every object that touches a picked one (supported types: line, polyline, circle, arc, attdef, text, mtext, ellipse, image), and when FSMODE is on must extend the set to objects touching those, chained until none remain, and be usable transparently at Select Objects prompts.
notes: Added from help page "FS (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw three lines joined end to end plus one isolated line, run FS on the first with FSMODE=0 and assert only its direct neighbour is added; with FSMODE=1 assert all three joined lines are selected and the isolated one is not.

statement: The Express Tool GATTE must globally replace the value of a chosen attribute tag in every insertion of a specified block (picked or named) with one new value.
notes: Added from help page "GATTE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Insert a block three times with tag NAME holding different values, run GATTE, pick the block and tag NAME, enter 'X1' and assert all three attributes now read X1.

statement: The Express Tool GETSEL must collect all objects matching a layer and object type, each chosen by picking a sample object or accepting the all-wildcard default, and leave them as the previous selection set for the next command.
notes: Added from help page "GETSEL (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: With lines and circles on LAYER1 and LAYER2, run GETSEL, pick a LAYER1 object then a line, then start MOVE and enter P and assert only the lines on LAYER1 are selected.

statement: The Express Tool IMAGEAPP must let the user name the raster editing application used by IMAGEEDIT, or enter a period to use the system default.
notes: Added from help page "IMAGEAPP (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run IMAGEAPP, enter the path of an editor executable and assert a following IMAGEEDIT launches that executable; enter '.' and assert the system default is used.

statement: The Express Tool IMAGEEDIT must launch the editor chosen by IMAGEAPP (or the system default) on the file of a selected image.
notes: Added from help page "IMAGEEDIT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select an attached image, run IMAGEEDIT and assert the configured editor process is started with that image file as its argument.

statement: The program must supply the Julian date utility set, including a DATE tool that shows the current date and time and AutoLISP functions converting between calendar and Julian dates and returning the weekday of a Julian day.
notes: Added from help page "JULIAN (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Evaluate (ctoj 1957 10 4 19 26 24) and then (jtoc) on the result; the round trip returns the original calendar date and time.

statement: The program must provide a layout merge tool that combines named layouts (with wildcard support) into a destination layout, creates a saved view and a labeled rectangle on the DEFPOINTS layer for each merged layout, optionally deletes the emptied layouts, and reassigns object handles.
notes: Added from help page "LAYOUTMERGE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run -LAYOUTMERGE with Layout1,Layout2 into Combined and answer Y to delete unused layouts; Combined holds both layouts' content with two saved views and Layout1 and Layout2 are removed.

statement: The program must provide an Express Tool that lists the AutoLISP-defined commands, functions or variables on request, or opens the application loader.
notes: Added from help page "LSP (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Define (defun c:foo () nil) and run LSP then Commands; foo appears in the list.

statement: The program must provide an Express Tool dialog that reads an AutoLISP file and displays its individual functions, with start and end line numbers and a choice of showing the header, the body, or both.
notes: Added from help page "LSPSURF (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run LSPSURF on a file with two defuns and select the second with Header Only; only its header and line numbers are displayed.

statement: The program must create a linetype definition from selected drawn objects, including text and shapes for complex linetypes, and store it in a chosen LIN file.
notes: Added from help page "MKLTYPE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a dash, a gap and a text item, run MKLTYPE on them, and confirm a new linetype entry is written to the LIN file and loads with the text element.

statement: The program must create a shape definition from selected geometry, splitting into sub-shapes when the size limit is exceeded and ignoring points and zero-length segments.
notes: Added from help page "MKSHAPE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a small polyline outline, run MKSHAPE, and confirm a shape with the chosen name can be inserted via SHAPE.

statement: The program must provide a combined Express Tool command that moves, copies, rotates and dynamically scales selected objects, with base point change and undo.
notes: Added from help page "MOCORO (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run MOCORO on a circle, Copy to two points, Rotate, and Undo the last step, confirming object count and orientation after each.

statement: The program must let the user set a folder for backup files so each save places the BAK file there, with a period clearing the setting.
notes: Added from help page "MOVEBAK (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run MOVEBAK with folder C:\bak, save a drawing twice, and confirm the BAK appears in that folder; enter . and confirm BAK returns to the drawing folder.

statement: The program must edit multiple polylines in one command, optionally converting selected lines and arcs to polylines, with the standard PEDIT options such as close, join, width, fit and spline.
notes: Added from help page "MPEDIT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select three polylines with MPEDIT, choose Width 2, and confirm all three have width 2.

statement: The program must stretch objects using several crossing windows or crossing polygons chosen in one command, with an undo option.
notes: Added from help page "MSTRETCH (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Use MSTRETCH with two crossing windows over different line ends, displace by (10,0), and confirm both ends moved while others stayed.

statement: PLT2DWG must import a legacy HPGL plot file into the current drawing preserving pen colors, prompting for the file name, and rejecting device-dependent HPGL/2 files.
notes: Added from help page "PLT2DWG (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run PLT2DWG on an HPGL file with two pen colors and assert geometry is created with those two colors.

statement: PROPULATE must update, list or clear Drawing Properties fields in one drawing or a folder of drawings from a template, using literal strings, title block attribute values and lists of xrefs, images and fonts.
notes: Added from help page "PROPULATE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run PROPULATE with a template mapping a title-block attribute to the Title property on two drawings and assert each drawing's Title property equals its attribute value.

statement: PSBSCALE must set or update the scale of selected blocks relative to paper space, so blocks inserted in model space appear at the requested paper-space size and can be re-adjusted after the viewport zoom changes.
notes: Added from help page "PSBSCALE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Insert a block in a 1:50 viewport, run PSBSCALE with factor 1 and assert the block is scaled 50 in model space; change the viewport scale and run Update to assert it adjusts.

statement: PSTSCALE must set or update text and mtext in model space so that it appears at a chosen paper-space height inside a layout viewport, compensating for the viewport scale and honoring a justification base point.
notes: Added from help page "PSTSCALE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In a viewport at 1:50, run PSTSCALE on a model-space text, choose Set with height 3.5 and justification Existing; the text's model height becomes 175 so it plots at 3.5 units, and after changing the viewport scale choosing Update restores 3.5.

statement: QLATTACH is an obsolete express tool that must attach a leader line to a selected mtext, tolerance or block reference object.
notes: Added from help page "QLATTACH (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run QLATTACH, select an mtext and pick a leader start point; a leader line is created attached to that mtext.

statement: QLATTACHSET is an obsolete express tool that must attach leader lines in bulk to a selection of mtext, tolerance or block reference objects.
notes: Added from help page "QLATTACHSET (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select five mtext objects and run QLATTACHSET; each of the five gets an attached leader line.

statement: QLDETACHSET is an obsolete express tool that must detach leader lines from a selected set of mtext, tolerance or block reference objects.
notes: Added from help page "QLDETACHSET (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: With leaders attached to three mtext objects, select them and run QLDETACHSET; the leaders remain but are no longer associated with the mtext, which can be moved independently.

statement: QQUIT must close every open drawing, offering to save each modified one (prompting for a name if unnamed), and then exit the application.
notes: Added from help page "QQUIT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: With two modified drawings open, run QQUIT and answer Yes to each save prompt; both files are saved and the application exits.

statement: REDIR must find and replace directory names in the hard-coded paths of xrefs, images, shapes, styles and rtext (limited by REDIRMODE), supporting a ? listing, partial-string replacement and stripping of all paths so files are found via the search path.
notes: Added from help page "REDIR (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: An xref attached from I:\WORK\TEST\ is changed by REDIR with old 'I:\WORK\TEST\' and new 'K:\TEST'; the xref path now reads under K:\TEST, and entering '*' with an empty replacement leaves only file names.

statement: REDIRMODE must set which object types (styles, xrefs, images, rtext) REDIR operates on, accepting abbreviated comma-separated names or * and offering a dialog and a command-line variant.
notes: Added from help page "REDIRMODE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run REDIRMODE and enter 'xref,sty'; the prompt reports 'Styles,Xrefs' and a following REDIR leaves images and rtext paths untouched.

statement: REPURLS must find and replace a full or partial URL string in the hyperlinks attached to all selected objects in one operation.
notes: Added from help page "REPURLS (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select objects whose hyperlinks use '.com' URLs and run REPURLS replacing '.com' with '.net'; all their hyperlink URLs now end in '.net'.

statement: The program must provide the REVERT express tool that closes and reopens the current drawing from disk, asking for confirmation first if there are unsaved changes.
notes: Added from help page "REVERT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a line without saving, run REVERT, answer to discard, and assert the drawing is reloaded from the saved file without the new line.

statement: The program must provide the RTEDIT express tool to edit an existing remote text object, changing its style, height, rotation, or its file or DIESEL source.
notes: Added from help page "RTEDIT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create an rtext object, run RTEDIT, set height to 0.5, and assert the object's height property is 0.5.

statement: The program must provide the RTEXT express tool to create remote text objects whose displayed content is read live from an external text file or a DIESEL expression, with style, height and rotation options.
notes: Added from help page "RTEXT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create an rtext with the File option pointing to a text file, change the file contents, regenerate, and assert the displayed text updates.

statement: The program must provide the RTUCS express tool to rotate the UCS dynamically with the pointing device about a highlighted active axis in increments of a set angle.
notes: Added from help page "RTUCS (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run RTUCS with angle 15 on the X axis, move the pointer to advance two increments, and assert the UCS is rotated 30 degrees about X.

statement: The program must provide the SAVEALL express tool to save every open drawing while leaving them open, prompting for a file name for any unnamed drawing.
notes: Added from help page "SAVEALL (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open two modified drawings, one unnamed, run SAVEALL, and assert both are written and a name is prompted for the unnamed one.

statement: The program must provide the SHOWURLS express tool to list all URLs attached to objects in the drawing and let the user view, edit or replace them.
notes: Added from help page "SHOWURLS (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Attach URLs to two objects, run SHOWURLS, replace one with a new address, and assert that object's URL is updated.

statement: The program must provide the SHP2BLK express tool to convert all instances of a selected shape into instances of a newly defined equivalent block.
notes: Added from help page "SHP2BLK (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Insert two instances of a shape, run SHP2BLK naming a block, and assert both are replaced by block references to the new block.

statement: The program must provide the SSX express tool to build a selection set from objects that match a selected template object, with an adjustable filter list of matching properties.
notes: Added from help page "SSX (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a red circle as template with the color filter active, run SSX, and assert all red circles in the drawing are selected.

statement: The program must provide the SUPERHATCH express tool to fill an area through a dialog using a chosen wipeout, xref, block or image as the hatch pattern.
notes: Added from help page "SUPERHATCH (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run SUPERHATCH with a block as the source, pick an internal point of a closed boundary, and assert the area is filled with the block pattern.

statement: The program must provide the SYSVDLG Express Tool, a dialog that lists system variables with wildcard filtering, validates edited values, shows current and initial values, blocks edits to read-only variables, and saves or restores variable sets from files.
notes: Added from help page "SYSVDLG (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open SYSVDLG, filter by DIM*, set DIMSCALE to 2, accept, and assert DIMSCALE reads 2 while a read-only variable's edit field is disabled.

statement: The program must provide the TCASE Express Tool, with dialog and command-line (-TCASE) forms, that converts the letter case of dimension text, attributes, mtext and text objects that are selected to sentence, lower, upper, title or toggle case.
notes: Added from help page "TCASE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a text object reading 'hello WORLD', run -TCASE Upper, and assert it reads 'HELLO WORLD'.

statement: The program must provide the TCIRCLE Express Tool to enclose each selected text or mtext object in a circle, slot or rectangle, sized by an offset factor and either variable per object or held constant at the largest enclosure.
notes: Added from help page "TCIRCLE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run TCIRCLE with offset factor 0.35 and Circle on two texts of different length and assert each gets an enclosing circle sized to its own extents.

statement: The program must provide the TEXTFIT Express Tool that stretches or compresses the width of a single-line text object so it spans new start and end points, and applies only to text, not mtext.
notes: Added from help page "TEXTFIT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run TEXTFIT on a text and give new endpoints 10 units apart and assert the text's rendered width becomes 10.

statement: The program must provide the TEXTMASK Express Tool that places an opaque mask behind selected text or mtext, offset by a given amount and grouped with the text, to hide underlying objects.
notes: Added from help page "TEXTMASK (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a line under a text, run TEXTMASK with offset 0.1 and assert a wipeout-style mask grouped with the text now hides the line portion beneath it.

statement: The program must provide the TEXTUNMASK Express Tool that removes the mask created by TEXTMASK from selected text or mtext.
notes: Added from help page "TEXTUNMASK (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Apply TEXTMASK to a text, run TEXTUNMASK on it, and assert the mask object is gone and underlying objects show again.

statement: The program must provide the TFRAMES Express Tool that toggles whether frames are shown on every image and wipeout object in the drawing.
notes: Added from help page "TFRAMES (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run TFRAMES with a wipeout and an image present and assert both frames toggle between visible and hidden.

statement: The program must provide the TJUST Express Tool to change the justification point of text, mtext or attribute definitions without moving the text visually.
notes: Added from help page "TJUST (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run TJUST on a left-justified text choosing MC and assert justification becomes middle-center and the text's rendered position is unchanged.

statement: The program must provide the TORIENT Express Tool to rotate text, mtext, attribute definitions and attributed blocks about their middle in 180-degree steps for best readability, or to set a specified absolute angle, without changing overall location.
notes: Added from help page "TORIENT (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select an upside-down text and run TORIENT Most Readable; assert rotation becomes 180 degrees different and the center point is unchanged.

statement: The program must provide the obsolete TREX Express Tool that combines trim (on pick) and extend (on Shift-pick) against selected edges while filtering out invalid edge types such as blocks and dimensions.
notes: Added from help page "TREX (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run TREX with one edge, pick a line crossing it to trim and Shift-pick a short line to extend, asserting both results.

statement: The program must provide the TSCALE Express Tool to scale text, mtext, attributes and attribute definitions by factor or to a final height, relative to existing or chosen justification point.
notes: Added from help page "TSCALE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a text of height 2 and run TSCALE with Height 4 and assert its height is 4 with its justification point unchanged.

statement: The program must report the scale of the active viewport, or of a chosen layout viewport while in paper space, formatted as PS:MS ratio plus an architectural, engineering or plain scale string depending on units.
notes: Added from help page "VPSCALE (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In a layout with architectural units and a 1/8"=1'-0" viewport, run VPSCALE, pick the viewport and assert output shows ratio 1:96 and that scale text.

statement: The program must align the views of selected adjacent layout viewports to a master viewport so all use the master's zoom factor and look like one continuous view.
notes: Added from help page "VPSYNC (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create two adjacent viewports, run VPSYNC choosing one as master and the other as child, and assert the child's scale and aligned view match the master.

statement: The program must attach extended data to a selected object under a chosen application name, using typed items such as string, integer, long, real, distance, scale, layer, handle, position, displacement and direction.
notes: Added from help page "XDATA (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run XDATA on a line with app name MYAPP and an ST value Sewer, then run XDLIST and assert the string Sewer is stored under MYAPP.

statement: The program must list the extended data attached to a selected object, either for one application name or all applications.
notes: Added from help page "XDLIST (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Attach xdata for two apps to a line, run XDLIST with Enter for all, and assert both applications' data are listed; give one name and assert only it.

statement: The program must report the type, block name, layer, linetype and color for a nested object chosen inside a block or xref, shown in a dialog, with a command-line counterpart.
notes: Added from help page "XLIST (Express Tool)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Pick a nested line within a block on layer WALLS using XLIST and assert the report shows type Line, the block name and layer WALLS.
